role: Maintainer's own change procedure: no outside contributions, gates are the reviewer, build/test commands, budgets, file registration, localization, PR steps, style, privacy-change rule.

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu
units.does: No outside contributions; PolyForm Strict license; Linux gates run on every push to main and every pull request (gates.yml triggers: push to main, pull_request, workflow_dispatch); Xcode work runs only on demand; points to docs/MAINTAINERS.md (exists).

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > The one rule that matters
units.does: Every gate enforced, none waived; zero swiftlint:disable directives in Emuqu/Sources — verified by grep (0 hits).

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > Before you start
units.does: `make setup-hooks` (→ scripts/install-git-hooks.sh) installs .githooks/pre-commit, where SwiftLint errors block and swiftformat runs in --lint mode only; `make codemap-setup` installs the pinned tree-sitter the code map needs, and the hook fails without it. A SwiftLint error or a stale code-map record blocks the commit. gates.yml runs script gates on push.

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > While you work
units.does: Build and unit-test commands via xcodebuild; warnings are errors — SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS = YES at project-level Debug and Release (project.pbxproj:4763,4822).

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > While you work > The code map is part of the change
units.does: Says every function, script target, workflow step and doc section has a record in docs/codemap/records and that CI, make ci and the pre-commit hook fail until the records for a change are current. Steps: impact before the change (make codemap-impact or codemap.py impact <path::key>); make the change; make codemap-guard and rewrite each listed record, removing fixed flags; re-read each re-check caller (codemap.py status lists them) and change it or its record if its behaviour changed; stamp after re-reading, callees before callers; lowering .ci/codemap_open_high.txt or .ci/codemap_open_med.txt when a high/medium finding is fixed. Links docs/codemap/README.md. Every command named exists.

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > While you work > Budgets ratchet down, never up
units.does: .ci/*.txt budgets (shared_usage, try_optional, legacy_observable_object, swiftlint_warning, unchecked_sendable, etc. — all exist) ratchet down. Raising a ceiling or lowering a min_* floor needs a `budget-raise-ok: .ci/<name>.txt <reason>` trailer in a commit in the compared range (path exact, reason free text — check_budget_monotonicity.sh is_allowed). gates.yml enforces it: on a push to main against the tip before the push, on a pull request against the target branch. Locally `make budget-monotonicity` (Makefile, baseline ${BUDGET_BASE_REF:-HEAD}) compares the working tree with HEAD, catching an uncommitted raise but not seeing an uncommitted trailer or an already-committed raise; `BUDGET_BASE_REF=origin/main make budget-monotonicity` checks committed work.

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > While you work > Adding a new Swift file
units.does: New Swift files under Emuqu, EmuquTests or EmuquUITests must be registered at PBXBuildFile, PBXFileReference, group children, Sources phase; `make orphan-swift-guard` (check_no_orphan_swift.sh) fails on files missing from the project. EmuquWatch Watch App is a PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup: files there are members by being on disk and must not be registered by hand, since a second entry fails with 'Multiple commands produce' (the orphan guard skips synchronised roots). Paths with '+' must be quoted.

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > While you work > Adding user-facing text
units.does: Strings localized into 17 languages (Localizable.xcstrings has 17 locales incl. en) with 100% coverage enforced; String(localized:bundle:) with LanguageManager.appBundle (LanguageManager.swift:36) and `make localization-bundle-guard` (Makefile:114); health copy linted by Tools/copy_linter/lint.py via `make copy-perimeter` (Makefile:171).

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > Before you open a pull request
units.does: `make ci` is the enforcement: gates.yml runs bash/python gates on push incl. debt budgets and spec conformance; build/tests/SwiftLint need macOS and run on demand; `make ci` runs lint, budgets, spec conformance, localization, copy perimeter, doc links and the full test suite with coverage (Makefile ci). Says two ci.yml checks are not in `make ci`: `make thread-sanitizer` and `make release-build`, to run when a change touches concurrency or could differ under the optimizer. Adds that `make codemap-impact` lists everything the branch's changes can affect and that a pull request gets the same list in the gates.yml job summary.
calls: .github/workflows/gates.yml::step script-gates/Code map impact of this pull request

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > Style
units.does: Style: docs/REFACTOR_SPEC.md is the standard and `make spec-conformance` (check_refactor_spec_conformance.sh) enforces declarations <=20 lines, nesting <=2, no commented-out code, no empty catches; written waivers for length and nesting are counted against the ratcheting .ci/spec_justified_* budgets, so a new waiver is a budget raise needing the budget-raise-ok trailer.

units.key: § How a change lands in Emuqu > Security and privacy
units.does: no behavioural claim: report vulnerabilities privately; any change to off-device data must update consent, privacy manifest, policy and App Store Connect together.
